problem: How many different arrangements of gold, silver, and bronze medalists can there be out of $10$ Olympic athletes, assuming there are no ties?

feedback.problem: A network TV scheduler has $30$ shows to choose from to make the network's prime-time lineup of shows.  The prime-time lineup will consist of $4$ shows. How many different lineups are possible?
feedback.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $30$ shows to choose from, so $n=30.$ We want to select $4$ of those shows for the lineup, so we have $r=4.$ 

Therefore, the number of different possible lineups is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{30}{P}_{4} & =\frac{30!}{(30-4)!} \\  & =\frac{30!}{26!} \\  & =\frac{30\cdot 29\cdot 28\cdot 27\cdot \cancel{26!}}{\cancel{26!}} \\  & =30\cdot 29\cdot 28\cdot 27 \\  & =657\,720.\end{aligned}
$$
